english.title: Use language intimating article / service etc can be got within Parliamnet Square other than in accordance with licence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used language within the central garden of Parliament Square which publicly intimated that an article, commodity, facility or service, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE ETC..) could be obtained within the Square or elsewhere, other than in accordance with the terms of a written licence issued by the Mayor or a person authorised by the Mayor to issue such a licence in that **(..SPECIFY BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaw 6(1)(d) of the Parliament Square Square Byelaws 2012 and section 385(3) of the Greater London Authority Act 1999.

english.notes:
(i) See byelaw 9 where a person must, on demand, provide their name and address should an authorised person have reasonable ground to believe a person has contravened the byelaws. (ii) See section 380 of the Greater London Authority Act 1999 for delegation of authority to grant permission to conduct this action.
(iii) See byelaw 7 for the power to seize and retain anything of a non-perishable nature used in connection with a breach of byelaw 6.
(iv) Byelaw 6(1) is a trading byelaw for the purposes of section 385 of the Act.
(v) See byelaw 8 for the power for the courts to make an order providing for the forfeiture of an item seized under byelaw 7(1) that was used in the commission of the offence when a person is convicted of the offence.
